title: Payoff Statements and Release of the Deed of Trust — Rural Home Loans
content:
**Terms.** A payoff statement for a Rural Home Loans loan, for the payoff date the member names, states unpaid fees, unpaid billed interest, interest from the first day of the payoff month through the payoff date at the note rate on 365 days, and the principal balance; the escrow balance is not netted against the payoff but refunded separately within the product's surplus refund days after payoff. There is no prepayment penalty and no fee for the statement. The statement is good through the product's payoff statement validity number of calendar days after its date, the statement date being day 0. The loan is paid off on the effective date of the payment that brings principal, interest and fees to zero, and the deed of reconveyance is sent for recording within the product's lien release days.

## Statement items

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Unpaid fees | as on the loan |
| Unpaid billed interest | as on the loan |
| Interest for the payoff month | from the first day of the payoff month through the payoff date, at the note rate, on 365 days |
| Principal | the principal balance |
| Prepayment penalty | none |
| Statement fee | none |
| Escrow balance | not netted; refunded separately |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A payoff dated the 10th of a month on a principal balance of 146000.00 USD at a note rate of 6.0 percent: the days from the first through the 10th are 10, and the interest is 146000.00 multiplied by 6.0, divided by 100, divided by 365 and multiplied by 10, that is 240.00 USD.

## Status change

The loan moves to paid off — from active, forbearance or nonaccrual — on the effective date of the payment that brings principal, interest and fees to zero.
